text: ArtCraft 为 DSH 提供一组面向 CAD、表格、音频、图片、视频、PDF、演示文稿和文档等创作应用的插件。每个 craft 插件把对应应用的命令行和 MCP 服务接入 DSH，注册命令搜索、参数查询、执行、检查和格式转换等工具，也可列出并调用应用自带的 MCP 工具。执行结果可附带渲染预览；适合希望让 agent 操作本机创作软件并产出或检查文件的用户。使用前需安装对应 craft CLI；支持的应用和命令因插件而异。

ArtCraft connects DSH agents to CAD, spreadsheet, audio, image, video, PDF, presentation, and document apps. Plugins search and run app commands, inspect files, convert formats, and call app MCP tools; results can include previews. Install the relevant craft CLI to operate its application and files.

ArtCraft 的功能「应用命令工具」：按关键词或分组搜索应用命令，并查询命令所需的参数格式，再通过 run 工具执行一个或多个操作。
ArtCraft 的功能「应用 MCP 桥接」：列出创作应用 MCP 服务提供的工具及其参数 schema，并调用指定工具；支持的应用还可连接已打开的应用窗口。
ArtCraft 的功能「检查与格式转换」：对支持的文件类型读取文档摘要，或将文档从一种格式转换为另一种格式，并返回 CLI 输出。
ArtCraft 的功能「渲染预览」：执行写入操作后可生成文档预览图像，并在附件服务可用时将图像附加到工具结果。
ArtCraft 的功能「后台长任务」：耗时操作可在后台继续运行；工具返回任务标识后，可查询状态、等待完成或终止任务。
ArtCraft 的工具通过对应创作应用的 CLI 工作；需要先在本机安装所选 craft 的命令行程序，插件会在调用时查找该程序。

dsh-artcraft README · What this is：The ArtCraft suite is fourteen native Rust applications. Each one already ships a headless CLI and
its own MCP server — but nothing tells an agent they exist, what they can do, or how to call them.

This repository closes that gap. Each app becomes a **DSH plugin** that registers model-callable
tools on `ctx.tools`, discovers the app's binary on your machine, and drives it as an external
process.

dsh-artcraft README · What this is：**No craft source is ever modified.** Every plugin lives here. The applications are dependencies,
not forks.

dsh-artcraft README · The fourteen：<sub>Command counts are read live from each binary; MCP counts are what each server declares.</sub>

dsh-artcraft README · Two surfaces per craft：**Modelled operations** with real JSON Schemas, served over JSON-RPC by the app itself. ``` gridcraft_mcp_tools {"search": "range"} gridcraft_mcp_call {"tool": "write_range", "arguments": {"range": "A1", "values": [["x"]]}} The MCP server is spawned once per plugin and kept warm — starting GridCraft's engine costs ~600 ms — then shut down after five idle minutes or when the plugin unloads.

dsh-artcraft README · What else the bridge gives you：- **Look at the result.** A render, screenshot or page image comes back as a file and a path;
  the agent opens it with `read_image`, so a visual task is checked instead of assumed.
- **Work in the open window.** Twelve of the fourteen publish a control channel, so pass
  `attach: <port>` to an MCP call and the agent edits the document the user already has open,
  with every change visible in the app. LightCraft and PdfCraft are headless only.
- **Use the app's own recipes.** `<craft>_mcp_tools` also lists the MCP **resources** (the open
  document, the command catalogue, comments) and **prompts** — FigCraft ships six curated
  workflows such as `design_system` and `prototype_flow`.
- **Watch the document change.** After a call writes a document, the plugin renders it with the
  application's own renderer and returns the image with the result, so each step of the work is
  visible in the transcript. The same render feeds a local panel (`node scripts/preview/server.mjs`,
  then open `http://127.0.0.1:4177`) showing the step list, the current page and a filmstrip of the
  ones before it; `dsh-artcraft-preview-panel` embeds that pan

dsh-artcraft README · Verify it yourself：```sh
node scripts/verify.mjs
```

Every craft must locate its binary, load its live catalog, expose the right tool set, complete an
MCP handshake, and produce a non-empty artifact from a real headless run:

```
cadcraft       v0.16.0   449 commands   12 MCP tools   ok
gridcraft      v0.15.0   364 commands   22 MCP tools   ok
soundcraft     v0.16.0   479 commands   17 MCP tools   ok
photocraft     v0.19.0   953 commands   26 MCP tools   ok

dsh-artcraft README · How it works：Each craft is described **once**, in
[`dsh-plugins/craft-kit/src/profiles.mjs`](dsh-plugins/craft-kit/src/profiles.mjs). The kernel turns
that description into tools and hides every difference between the apps:

dsh-artcraft README · How it works：| Craft | How a headless run is spelled |
|:--|:--|
| GridCraft, CADCraft, DeckCraft, WordCraft, SoundCraft, DesignCraft | `--cmd 'id={...}'` |
| PhotoCraft, VectorCraft | `--cmd id --params '{...}'` |
| LightCraft, PdfCraft | positional `id key=value` |
| EffectCraft | positional `id {...}` |
| FilmCraft | a generated JSONL script file |

dsh-artcraft README · How it works：```
dsh-plugins/
├── craft-kit/              shared kernel
│   ├── src/                discovery · exec · catalogs · tool factory · MCP client
│   ├── lib/                generated plain ESM

Every fact about the binaries was **measured by running them**, never assumed. Where a craft's real
CLI contradicted an expectation, the raw output is recorded in [docs/craft-notes/](docs/craft-notes).

dsh-artcraft README · Beyond the fourteen：All **23** repositories matching `craft` under `github.com/storytold` were cloned and assessed
([docs/CRAFT-MATRIX.md](docs/CRAFT-MATRIX.md)). Fourteen are applications with a published headless
CLI and became plugins. The other eleven are libraries, asset bundles, or GUIs without a scriptable
entry point — including `artcraft`, the umbrella app, whose MCP support is a documented UI stub.

dsh-artcraft README · Contributing：Found a craft whose CLI behaves differently than described? The notes are meant to be corrected —
open an issue with the raw output, or run the offending command with tracing on:

```sh

dsh-artcraft README · macOS / Linux：DSH_ARTCRAFT_TRACE=/tmp/trace.log node scripts/verify.mjs <craft>
```

```powershell

dsh-artcraft README · Windows (PowerShell)：$env:DSH_ARTCRAFT_TRACE = "$env:TEMP\artcraft-trace.log"; node scripts\verify.mjs <craft>
```

That writes the exact argv of every invocation to the trace file.
